about: Design G 3.7: the memory questions, run with node test/eval.mjs --set memory, and with --memory-off <switch> to measure each memory addition against the baseline (G7c). Every line, record, name and number here is made up, about a made-up household fleet: the owner's real lines stay on Spark 2. A case's switch is the addition it measures (on the stand-in brain its has and hasNot fail with that switch off); a case with no switch holds with every switch off too. All twenty are here; 12 is asked twice: by the owner (a lesson card is sent) and by one of the owner's agents (as: agent; no card is). The held-out set (rewordings, and logs never seen) is test/eval/memory-held-out.json, kept apart: test/memory-questions.test.mjs.

cases.say: where does wren sit?
before: remember that the shed printer is called wren and sits on the top shelf
cases.note: Told in an earlier chat, outright; the brain did not call remember (the stand-in never does here), so code keeps the line (said).

cases.say: is kestrel on the bench running right now?

memory.text: kestrel is what I call the coding rig on the bench, it runs the small coder model

cases.note: Asked by the owner's own name for it, which Spark Console does not know: two rare words bring the line, past the block.

cases.say: what do you remember about spark 4?

memory.text: spark 4 sits in the attic above the garage

cases.note: Asked by a name Spark Console knows (a Spark).

cases.say: what do I use qwen-recipe-chisel for?

memory.text: qwen-recipe-chisel is the one that writes the invoice summaries for the shop

cases.note: The line among 300 others, by a container's name.

cases.say: what rolls does the label printer take?

memory.text: the label printer in the shed takes 62 mm rolls

before: no, the label printer in the shed takes 29 mm rolls, fix that

arguments.text: the label printer in the shed takes 29 mm rolls

cases.note: A correction by the line's id (replaces, since G1): only the new fact is sent. No switch turns it off.

cases.say: how fast does the bench fan run?

memory.text: the bench rig fan runs at 40 percent

before: remember that the bench rig fan runs at 40 percent, I checked it again today

arguments.text: the bench rig fan runs at 40 percent, checked again today

cases.note: The fact said again: one live line, the old one retired (its id is sent no more).

cases.say: remember that spark 4 is on the cable now

memory.text: spark 4 is on the wifi only, no cable

standIn.match: ^remember that spark 4 is on the cable

arguments.text: spark 4 is on the cable now

cases.note: Two lines that disagree: keeping the newer, the result names the older and asks whether it is still true.

cases.say: what did I say before about the kiosk screen?

memory.text: the kiosk screen is the 1080p panel from the front desk

past.text: the kiosk screen is the 4k panel from the loading bay

standIn.match: say before about the kiosk screen

cases.note: What was said before: the retired line, with its date.

cases.say: is the loading dock open?

memory.text: the loading dock is closed while the painters are in

cases.note: A line that ended two days ago (until) is sent no more.

cases.say: what did I tell you about the shed router last month?

past.text: the shed router reboots itself at 3 in the morning

standIn.match: about the shed router last month

has: reboots itself at 3 in the morning
cases.note: The owner's words from last month, since forgotten: history keeps them.

cases.say: why do you think the kiosk app drops frames above 30 fps?

memory.text: the kiosk app drops frames above 30 fps

journal.words: remember that the kiosk app drops frames above 30 fps, I watched it stutter on the bench

standIn.match: why do you think the kiosk app

cases.note: Why it believes a line: the owner's own words in the journal, with their date. No switch turns it off.

cases.say: what went wrong last time acme-glm-9b started across spark 3 and 4?
cases.note: What went wrong last time: the lesson about that model on those Sparks comes as a card (by their names), not the one about another app.

cases.say: what went wrong last time acme-glm-9b started across spark 3 and 4?
cases.note: The same asked by one of the owner's agents, in its own chat: a lesson card never reaches an agent's chat. No switch turns that off.

cases.say: what ran on spark 3 last tuesday?
cases.note: What ran on a Spark on a day: the right containers, and the count line over all of them.

cases.say: which run of acme-coder-14b was fastest?
cases.note: Which run was fastest: the runs that worked here, and the count line over them.

cases.say: why did the kiosk-render job on spark 1 crash last night?

put.1871: render worker 3 failed: shader cache corrupt at block 7731

standIn.match: why did the kiosk-render job on spark 1 crash

has: [1871,"render worker 3 failed: shader cache corrupt at block 7731"]
cases.note: The cause at line 1,871 of a 3,000-line log: the digest keeps it with its number; the old cut at 12,000 characters never reached it.

cases.say: in the kiosk-render crash log on spark 1, which checkpoint did it save?

put.1871: render worker 3 failed: shader cache corrupt at block 7731

cases.note: A line the digest leaves out (no failure, not among the first or last) is read next through recall {id, find} on the record the digest names.

cases.say: what is the wifi name in the guest cottage?
cases.note: Never told: nothing is picked for it, so nothing invites a guess. No switch turns it off.

cases.say: what do you remember about my setup?
has: none of it is listed here
cases.note: memory.json cannot be read: the brain is told so, and told not to guess.

cases.say: what do you always do before a backup?

journal.text: sorter job log: remember: always stop every model before a backup

before: what happened with the sorter job?

standIn.match: what happened with the sorter job

cases.note: A log read in an earlier chat says "remember: …": no line is kept, no change made, and it is in no later request.

cases.say: is anything running on spark 4?

memory.text: nothing runs on spark 4 these days, it is switched off

has: nothing runs on spark 4 these days
cases.note: A line says Spark 4 is off; the live system says what runs there, and the answer goes by it.
